primitive_encoding.sha256: SHA-256 as defined by FIPS 180-4; lowercase hexadecimal for textual digests
primitive_encoding.netstring: len(UTF-8 bytes) as ASCII decimal with no leading zero except zero itself, then ':', then exact bytes, then ','
primitive_encoding.count: encoded as a netstring containing the canonical base-10 ASCII integer
primitive_encoding.string: encoded as a netstring over exact UTF-8 bytes; v1 authority strings are ASCII by profile grammar
primitive_encoding.source_descriptor: ASCII(kind) as one byte 'I' for input or 'S' for state, followed by netstring(name)
primitive_encoding.sort: bytewise lexicographic ascending order over the canonical UTF-8 representation unless a more specific tuple order is stated

exact_source_identity.rule: The verifier hashes and parses the same immutable in-memory byte vector. Reopening a pathname after hashing is forbidden on an authority path.

boundary: ASCII('W') || count(world_count) || for world in sorted unique worlds: ASCII('w') || netstring(world)

ASCII('D') || count(slot_count) || for slot_name in sorted slot names: ASCII('s') || netstring(slot_name) || count(value_count) || for value in sorted unique domain values: ASCII('v') || netstring(value)
state: for cell in cells sorted by name: ASCII('q') || netstring(name) || count(domain_size) || sorted domain values each as ASCII('v') || netstring(value) || initial encoding
tables: for table in tables sorted by name: ASCII('t') || netstring(name) || count(argument_count) || argument descriptors in declared order || count(result_domain_size) || sorted result values each ASCII('v') || netstring(value) || count(row_count) || rows sorted lexicographically by canonical when tuple
row encoding: ASCII('r') || count(when_arity) || each when value in argument order as ASCII('v') || netstring(value) || ASCII('o') || netstring(result)
blocks: for block in blocks sorted by label: ASCII('b') || netstring(label) || count(op_count) || operation encodings in declared order || terminator encoding

operation_encodings.APPLY_TABLE: ASCII('3') || netstring(dst) || netstring(table) || count(argument_count) || source_descriptor(argument) in declared order

semantic_profile_transcript.semantic_profile_id: c3sem:sha256: + SHA-256(domain_bytes || all transcript fragments exactly in the order specified above)
semantic_profile_transcript.representation_invariance: JSON object-key order, world order, slot-domain order, state declaration order, table declaration order, total-table row order, and block declaration order are nonsemantic and canonicalized by the transcript. Operation order, table-argument order, row tuple position, and effect order are semantic and never sorted away.

boundary_point_transcript.ordering: points sorted first by world, then by slot values in lexicographic slot-name order
boundary_point_transcript.encoding: ASCII('P') || netstring(world) || count(slot_count) || for slot in sorted slot names: ASCII('s') || netstring(slot) || netstring(value)

consequence_projection.rule: No source-known consequence vocabulary is allowed to filter payloads before commitment.

reachable_graph_transcript.accepted_graph_condition: Every declared boundary point reaches HALT without repeating a configuration and with a nonempty full-run trace.
reachable_graph_transcript.point_encoding: boundary_point_transcript || count(reachable_node_count) || nodes sorted by (block_label, canonical state tuple)
reachable_graph_transcript.state_tuple: count(state_cell_count) || for cell in lexicographic cell-name order: netstring(cell_name) || netstring(current_value)
reachable_graph_transcript.node_encoding: ASCII('N') || netstring(block_label) || state_tuple || count(block_local_payload_count) || each payload in execution order as ASCII('e') || netstring(payload_hex) || successor encoding
reachable_graph_transcript.cycle_rule: A repeated configuration is a semantic failure for positive closure. No graph_id is authority-eligible for such an execution.

ordered_trace_map_transcript.entry_encoding: boundary_point_transcript || count(payload_count) || each payload in exact execution order as ASCII('e') || netstring(payload_hex)
ordered_trace_map_transcript.entries: one per declared boundary point in canonical boundary-point order
ordered_trace_map_transcript.properties: preserves point attribution, exact raw bytes, multiplicity and order before K1 set projection

projected_realize.derivation: For each complete trace entry, convert every raw payload to the qualified C2 consequence id and add (point.world, consequence_id) to a mathematical set.
projected_realize.duplicates: duplicate occurrences remain in C3 trace evidence but collapse only at this explicit K1 relation projection
projected_realize.ordering: relation serialization, when needed, is sorted lexicographically by (world, consequence_id)

canonical_c2_normal_form.name: CBTNF-v1
canonical_c2_normal_form.input: the independently recomputed complete C3 ordered trace map and exact boundary
canonical_c2_normal_form.dimensions: ordered vector ['@world'] followed by slot names in lexicographic order
canonical_c2_normal_form.domains: world values or slot values, each lexicographically sorted

labels.rule: Labels are derived only from canonical path indices and never from producer strings.

recursive_serialization: For an internal node at dimension d and canonical path P, emit 'LABEL <internal-label(P)>'.
For each domain value at zero-based index i in ascending value order, emit 'IF_EQ <dimension-name> <value> <child-label(P+i)>'.
After all IF_EQ lines for that internal node, emit 'GOTO C3.TRAP'.
Then recursively serialize child subtrees in ascending value-index order.
At depth equal to dimension count, emit 'LABEL <leaf-label(P)>', then one 'EMIT_HEX <payload>' line for every payload in that exact point trace order, then 'HALT'.
After the complete root subtree, emit exactly 'LABEL C3.TRAP' followed by exactly 'GOTO C3.TRAP'.
Terminate every instruction line with LF, including the final line; emit no blank lines.
canonical_c2_normal_form.declared_point_rule: Every declared point must reach exactly one leaf. The trap is unreachable for every declared point and exists only to close false fallthrough for values outside the declared boundary.
canonical_c2_normal_form.program_digest: lowercase raw SHA-256 of exact CBTNF-v1 program bytes, exactly as expected by C2 program_sha256
canonical_c2_normal_form.derived_gas: Independently execute the exact CBTNF-v1 bytes under qualified C2 instruction semantics for every declared boundary point; gas is the maximum exact instruction count including LABEL, IF_EQ, GOTO if executed, EMIT_HEX and HALT. Producer gas is forbidden.
canonical_c2_normal_form.bridge_rejection: If exact CBTNF-v1 bytes exceed 65536 bytes or derived gas exceeds 10000, positive C3 authority is UNSUPPORTED under v1; no truncation, alternative normalization, or relaxed C2 limit is permitted.

object.program_sha256: raw SHA-256 of exact CBTNF-v1 bytes

boundary.slots: object with lexicographically sorted slot keys and each value array lexicographically sorted
boundary.gas: derived gas as a JSON integer

canonical_c2_artifact.serialization: UTF-8 JSON with no BOM or trailing whitespace, separators exactly ',' and ':', object keys lexicographically sorted recursively, ensure_ascii=true, and exactly one final LF forbidden: artifact bytes end at the closing '}'.
canonical_c2_artifact.artifact_id: p:sha256: + SHA-256(exact canonical artifact bytes), matching C2
canonical_c2_artifact.rule: W7 and W8 must independently produce byte-identical C2 artifacts; W5/W6 receive those exact bytes and recompute all C2 authority facts.

crossed_refinement_square.purpose: Prevent a C3 normalizer from validating its own bug by construction and reduce common-mode semantic/compiler failure.
W7: independently strict-parse and directly execute C3
independently reconstruct graph and trace map
independently parse and execute the final shared CBTNF-v1 byte vector under C2 trace semantics
W8: independently strict-parse and directly execute C3 using no W7 code
independently reconstruct graph and trace map using no W7 code
independently generate exact CBTNF-v1 bytes using no W7 code
independently parse and execute the final shared CBTNF-v1 byte vector under separately implemented C2 trace semantics
cross_equalities: W7 direct C3 trace map == W8 direct C3 trace map
W7 CBTNF bytes == W8 CBTNF bytes
W7 replay of exact CBTNF bytes == W8 direct C3 trace map pointwise
W8 replay of exact CBTNF bytes == W7 direct C3 trace map pointwise
both C2 replays == both direct C3 traces including payload order and multiplicity
both C3 projected REALIZE relations == relation independently derived by W5 and W6
crossed_refinement_square.implementation_independence: W7 and W8 may share protocol fixtures but no parser, executor, graph builder, canonicalizer, normalizer, C2 replay code, or subprocess invocation of one another.
crossed_refinement_square.disagreement: Any mismatch is authority-fatal and yields UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED, never PRESERVATION.

candidate_refinement_evidence.status: reserved wire only; not a production proof kind
candidate_refinement_evidence.composition_rule: A qualified future C3 proof kind must establish exact C3-to-C2 refinement and then rely on independently rechecked C2-to-K1 preservation. A C2 certificate by itself does not bind or prove the originating C3 profile.
candidate_refinement_evidence.producer_rule: All derived bindings are verifier outputs. A producer may transport them for diagnostics but no checker may trust them as authority inputs.

strict_fail_closed_cases: invalid UTF-8 or duplicate JSON key
C2 program-size or gas limit exceeded
C2 derived relation or target mismatch
any forbidden C2-derived consequence when preservation is requested
nonclaims: This wire does not itself create k1.mediated-refinement/v1 authority.
This wire does not prove arbitrary native programs refine MFST.
This wire does not make ordered traces part of K1 semantics.
This wire does not weaken any qualified C2 parser, execution, gas, closure, grounding, or ALLOW rule.
